statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the maximum possible minimum Manhattan distance: r = max { min { D(i,j) : i and j are in S and i < j } : S is a subset of {0,...,n-1} with |S| = k }. Equivalently, there exists a k-element index set S with D(i,j) >= r for all distinct i,j in S, and for every k-element index set T there exist distinct i,j in T with D(i,j) <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(points). For every i with 0 <= i < n, len(points[i]) = 2; write x_i = points[i][0], y_i = points[i][1], and D(i,j) = |x_i - x_j| + |y_i - y_j|. Assume 1 <= side <= 10^9, n <= 15000, 4 <= k <= min(25, n), n <= 4*side, 0 <= x_i <= side, 0 <= y_i <= side, each (x_i, y_i) lies on the boundary of the square (x_i = 0 or x_i = side or y_i = 0 or y_i = side), and (x_i, y_i) != (x_j, y_j) for every i != j.
